info.title: LDAP-Rest API
info.description: RESTful API for LDAP management with LDAP-Rest

post.description:
Forces an immediate reload of all token entries from the LDAP
branch configured via `--authz-dynamic-base`.

**Conditional registration:** this endpoint is only added to the
router when the server was started with
`--authz-dynamic-reload-endpoint true`.  It will be absent
(404) otherwise.

**Authentication required:** the request must carry a valid
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header that matches an existing
entry in the token cache.  An unauthenticated or unrecognised
token receives a `401` response.

On success the response includes the number of tokens now held
in the in-memory cache.  This count can be used to verify that
the expected entries are present after adding or removing tokens
in LDAP.

tokens.description: Number of token entries now in the cache.

401.description: Missing, invalid, or unrecognised bearer token.

get.summary: Administration scope of the current user
get.description:
Returns the branches the signed-in user administers, the permissions
held on each, and — per entity — whether they may create a new entry.
A client uses it to show the scope explicitly and to hide actions that
would be refused.

With no authorization plugin judging the caller the server grants
everything, and the answer says so through `unrestricted: true`.
When plugins judge the caller and none of them can describe a scope
(`authzPerRoute`, `authzDynamic`), the answer is `described: false`
with nothing in it: no model can say what will be granted, and a
client should not offer what it cannot know.

`sources` names the authorization plugins judging the caller, and
`source` the one this scope comes from — the first loaded, or the one
`--authz-scope-source` names — so a client can tell a scope from one
model among several from the server's whole answer.

`transit` is the transit branch (`--authz-transit-branch`) when the
describing plugin judges entries by their attachment, `null`
otherwise. Every administrator may put an entry they manage there,
and claim one from it into a branch they write.

`linksAnyDomain` says whether the caller may link an organization to
any mail domain, rather than only to those an organization above it
links: with `authzLinid1`, an administrator holding write on the top
organization or on `--authz-global-organization`. `true` when
unrestricted, `false` when the describing plugin cannot tell, and
when the scope is not described. Like the rest of the scope, it is
the answer of `source` alone: another authorization plugin judging
the same caller may still refuse the link — `authzPerBranch`
grants it on the top organization only.

`passwordPolicies` says whether the caller may list the password
policies (`GET /password-policies`), so a client offers them without
asking for them and being refused: the judgement the describing
plugin makes of a search of `--ppolicy-base` — with `authzLinid1`
and `--authz-global-branches` holding it, only those who read that
branch. `true` when unrestricted, `false` when the scope is not
described, and absent when `core/ldap/passwordPolicy` is not loaded.
It is the answer of `source` too: another authorization plugin
judging the same caller (`--authz-combine`) may still refuse the
listing, and so may a route-level gate (`authzPerRoute`).

Returns aggregated runtime configuration for all loaded plugins.
Plugins that declare the `configurable` role expose a named block
under `features` via their `getConfigApiData()` method.  The
response shape is open-ended (`additionalProperties: true`) because
the exact keys depend on which plugins are active.

Typical consumers include browser-embedded LDAP editors that need
to discover available schemas, endpoint prefixes, and feature flags
without hard-coding server topology.

Exists exclusively as a minimal example for plugin development. The handler fires the `hello` hook and collects the results from every registered listener into `hookResults`. In a production deployment this plugin is normally disabled; enabling it is safe but adds no functional value.

schema.description: Response returned by the hello-world demo endpoint.

hookResults.description: Results collected from every function registered on the `hello` hook. Empty when no hook listeners are installed.

post.summary: Set the lifecycle state of an account
post.description:
Moves the account to one of the states its schema declares —
`enabled`, `disabled`, or whatever else the deployment defines.
The state names come from the schema, so `GET /config` lists the
ones this directory accepts.

state.description: Name of a state declared by the schema.

post.summary: Reset the password of an account
post.description:
Replaces the credential. When the body carries no `password`, one
is generated and returned **once** in the response — it is never
readable afterwards. A `password` that is present must be a
non-empty string: an empty one is refused with a `400` rather
than silently replaced by a generated password the caller never
sees. When the schema declares a `passwordReset` attribute,
`forceChange` (true by default) also flags the account so the
directory asks for a new password at next login.

400.description: Empty, non-textual or too long password, a control character in it, or a non-boolean forceChange.

password.description: New password; generated when absent. An empty string and control characters are refused.

forceChange.description: Require a change at next login.

get.description:
Returns a CSV file with the header row listing all editable columns for
the `{resource}` type. Fixed, calculated, and organization-path columns
are excluded because they are injected automatically during import.

Use this template as the starting point for a bulk import file.

post.description:
Accepts a multipart/form-data upload containing a CSV file and optional
control flags. Each data row is mapped to an LDAP entry using the resource
schema. Multi-valued attributes can be expressed with semicolons
(`val1;val2;val3`). An `organizationDn` column (not listed in the template
header) may be provided to set the organization link and path attributes
automatically.

**Dry-run mode** (`dryRun=true`) validates, judges and counts rows without
writing to LDAP: a row the caller may not write fails as in an import.
`continueOnError` (default `true`) keeps processing subsequent rows
after an individual row fails.

400.description: No file uploaded or malformed request.

file.description: CSV file to import (max 10 MB by default).

dryRun.description: When true, validate and count rows without writing to LDAP.

updateExisting.description:
When true, existing entries are updated (replace). When false
(default), they are skipped.

continueOnError.description: Continue processing subsequent rows after a row-level error.

get.description:
Returns every group under the configured group base. The optional
`match` query is matched against the attributes named by
`attribute`, as a substring — the same semantics as the flat entity
lists. Without `attribute` it is either a raw LDAP filter (when it
contains `=`) or an exact value of the RDN attribute.

parameters.name: match
parameters.description: Substring to look for, LDAP filter, or exact value.

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description:
LDAP attribute name to match `match` against, as a substring.
Several may be given, separated by commas; a group matching any
of them is returned. Each name must be indexed for a substring
search, or the directory scans the branch.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of attributes to return.

get.description:
The `:cn` segment may be either the group's RDN value (e.g.
`admins`) or its full DN. Returns the raw LDAP entry.

400.description: A member does not exist or is not a DN; none is added.

member.description: One DN or a list of DNs to add.

delete.description: `:member` is the URL-encoded DN of the member to remove.

400.description: The member is the placeholder (`--group-dummy-user`), which cannot be removed.

409.description: The member is the last one of the group and no placeholder is configured to take its place.

post.description:
Only registered when both
`--ldap-organization-link-attribute` and
`--ldap-organization-path-attribute` are configured.

get.description:
Returns the single root organizational unit configured via
`--ldap-top-organization`. Authorization plugins may filter the result
to only the branches the caller has access to.

The `:dn` segment must be the URL-encoded fully-qualified DN of the
organizational unit (e.g. `ou=Engineering%2Cou=organizations%2Cdc%3Dexample%2Cdc%3Dcom`).
Returns a 404 when the DN does not exist or does not have
`objectClass=organizationalUnit`.

put.description:
Partial attribute update. Each key in the body replaces the existing
value for that attribute. The `ou` RDN and the organization path/link
attributes cannot be changed through this endpoint.

delete.description:
Deletes the organizational unit identified by `:dn`. The operation is
rejected with **409 Conflict** when any entry still references this
organization via the organization-link attribute (i.e. the OU is not
empty).

get.description:
Returns the direct child organizational units of `:dn`, followed by
up to `ldap_organization_max_subnodes` (default 50) entries (users,
groups) whose organization-link attribute points to it.

Two things bound the answer, and each appends a sentinel entry with
`objectClass: [moreIndicator]` and `_isMoreIndicator: "true"`, which
a client must drop before treating the rest as entries:

- the cap on the attached entries, whose sentinel is at
  `more-<dn>` and carries `_totalCount` and `_displayedCount`;
- a directory refusing to list a branch in one answer, whose
  sentinel is at `more-organizations-<dn>` and carries
  `_displayedCount` alone — nothing counted the rest.

Child organizations are not capped.

parameters.name: objectClass
parameters.description:
Filter linked entities by objectClass (e.g. `inetOrgPerson`,
`groupOfNames`). Pass `organizationalUnit` to return only child OUs.

get.description:
Full-text search across child OUs and linked entries (users, groups)
of `:dn`. The `q` parameter is matched against `ou`, `description`,
`uid`, `cn`, `sn`, `givenName`, and `mail`.

Matching attached entries are capped at
`ldap_organization_max_subnodes` (default 50), and the same sentinel
entries as `/subnodes` say when the answer is partial: a client must
drop whatever carries `_isMoreIndicator` before treating the rest as
entries.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search query matched against common attributes.

400.description: Query parameter `q` missing, or the DN cannot be parsed.

get.description:
Searches the organizations under `:dn`, at any depth, and `:dn`
itself. Unlike `/subnodes/search`, which only looks at the direct
children and mixes in the linked users and groups, this answers
organizations only: it is the call behind a department picker over
a tree too wide to list.

`q` is matched against `ou`, `description` and, when
`ldap_organization_path_attribute` is set, the path attribute, so a
query such as `Government / lin` finds a department by its path.

At most `ldap_organization_max_subnodes` (default 50) organizations
are returned. A partial answer ends with a sentinel entry at
`more-organizations-<dn>` carrying `_isMoreIndicator: "true"`, which
a client must drop before treating the rest as organizations, and
which says why the answer is partial:

- more organizations matched than the cap: it carries
  `_totalCount` and `_displayedCount`, and a narrower query helps;
- the directory refused to list them all: it carries
  `_displayedCount` alone — nothing counted the rest — and the fix
  is the size limit of the account ldap-rest binds as.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search query matched against name, description and path.

400.description: Query parameter `q` missing, or the DN cannot be parsed.

post.description:
Creates a new organizational unit. The `ou` field becomes the RDN.
`parentDn` controls where in the tree the node is placed; it defaults
to the configured top organization.

Performs an LDAP `modifyDN` to relocate the organizational unit `:dn`
under `targetOrgDn`. The new DN is returned in the response.
Moving into a descendant or the current parent is rejected.

200.description: Organization moved. Returns the new DN.

404.description: Source or target organization not found.

targetOrgDn.description: DN of the destination organizational unit.

get.description:
Returns the active OpenLDAP ppolicy configuration read from the DN
configured via `--ppolicy-default-dn`, or discovered by searching for
`objectClass=pwdPolicy` when that option is absent.
Results are cached for 60 seconds.

403.description: An authorization plugin keeps the policies from the caller.

get.description:
Returns the current password state for user `:id`. The `id` may be
a plain `uid` value or a full DN. The response is computed from the
user's ppolicy operational attributes combined with the active policy.

post.description:
Removes the `pwdAccountLockedTime` and `pwdFailureTime` operational
attributes from the user entry, effectively clearing the lockout state.
If the account was not locked the operation still succeeds (idempotent).

get.description:
Scans the user base for accounts whose password will expire within
`days` days. Results are sorted ascending by `daysUntilExpiration`.
Each account is judged by its own policy (`pwdPolicySubentry`, else
the default one); those whose policy sets no `pwdMaxAge` never appear.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Warning window in days (defaults to `--ppolicy-warn-days` or 14).

200.description: List of expiring accounts with their warning window.

get.description:
Returns all user entries in the user base that have a
`pwdAccountLockedTime` attribute set, regardless of whether the
lockout has expired. Use the `/unlock` endpoint to clear individual
lockouts.

Returns every `pwdPolicy` entry under `--ppolicy-base` (else
`--ldap-base`), sorted by `cn`, and the attributes a policy can be
given: those the API writes that the directory's schema defines.

post.description:
Creates `cn=<cn>` under `--ppolicy-base` (else `--ldap-base`), applied
to `userPassword`. The body holds `cn` and the attributes to set.

400.description: Missing `cn`, unknown attribute or wrongly typed value.

409.description: A policy of that name exists.

patch.description:
Sets the attributes the body names and removes those given `null`.
Writing `pwdCheckModuleArg` or `pwdUseCheckModule` gives the entry
the `pwdPolicyChecker` class when it lacks it.

400.description: Unknown or read-only attribute, or wrongly typed value.

delete.description:
Refused while the policy is the default one or an entry's
`pwdPolicySubentry` names it.

409.description: The policy is the default one, or is still applied.

put.summary: Assign a password policy to an account
put.description:
Sets the account's `pwdPolicySubentry` to the policy named `policy`,
or removes it when `policy` is `null`, the account then getting the
default policy. The `id` may be a plain `uid` value or a full DN.

404.description: No such account, or no policy of that name.

post.description:
Validates a candidate password against the locally-configured complexity
rules (`--ppolicy-min-length`, `--ppolicy-require-uppercase`, etc.).
This endpoint is only registered when `--ppolicy-validate-complexity` is
enabled. It does **not** call LDAP — it runs a local rule check only.

errors: At least one special character required

get.description:
Entry points of the low-level API: the subtrees the server is
configured to expose (`--ldap-raw-base`, defaulting to `--ldap-base`).

Server capabilities: naming contexts, supported controls, extensions
and the DN of the subschema entry. Read with the service account, as
directory metadata rather than user data.

Parsed content of the subschema entry: object classes (with their
`MUST`/`MAY` attributes and `SUP` chain), attribute types, syntaxes
and matching rules. Cached for `--ldap-raw-schema-cache-ttl` seconds.

Raw LDAP search. `base` must be inside one of the exposed bases, and
the usual authorization hooks apply on top of that.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: Search base. Defaults to the first exposed base.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries, capped by `--ldap-raw-max-results`.

400.description:
Invalid scope, invalid limit, or unparseable LDAP filter. The
message names the offending filter and recalls the expected
form, e.g. `Invalid LDAP filter "gov"`.

404.description: No such base, or one the caller cannot read: both answer alike.

get.summary: List the children of an entry
get.description:
Direct children (scope `one`) of the URL-encoded `:dn`, as needed to
expand a tree node. At most `--ldap-raw-max-results` entries are
returned; `truncated` tells whether the branch holds more.

parameters.name: children
parameters.description:
When set, each child is probed for children of its own so the UI
can decide whether to draw an expand arrow. Costs one extra
search per child.

get.description:
Full content of the URL-encoded `:dn`, operational attributes
included. Binary values are base64-encoded and flagged as such.
Attributes listed in `--ldap-raw-hidden-attribute` are omitted.

Returns a paginated list of SCIM User resources matching the optional
filter. Pagination is controlled by `startIndex` (1-based) and `count`.
The response always uses the `ListResponse` envelope.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
SCIM filter expression (RFC 7644 §3.4.2.2), e.g.
`userName eq "bjensen"` or `emails.value co "@example.com"`.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description: 1-based index of the first result to return.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return per page.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description:
Comma-separated SCIM attribute names to return, in place of the
default set (RFC 7644 section 3.9). Mutually exclusive with
`excludedAttributes`.

parameters.name: excludedAttributes
parameters.description: Comma-separated SCIM attribute names to exclude from the response.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Attribute to sort results by (parsed but sort not guaranteed server-side).

example.detail: Filter parse error: unexpected token near "eq"

post.description:
Creates a new SCIM User resource. The `userName` attribute is required.
Returns the created resource with status 201 and a `Location` header.

Location.description:
URI of the created resource (RFC 7644 section 3.1). Absolute
when `--scim-base-url` is set, prefix-relative otherwise.

400.description: Request body is missing or malformed.

409.description: A user with that userName already exists.

get.description:
Returns a single SCIM User resource. The `:id` value is the server-
assigned opaque identifier returned when the resource was created.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description:
Comma-separated attribute names to return, in place of the default
set (RFC 7644 section 3.9). Mutually exclusive with
`excludedAttributes`.

parameters.name: excludedAttributes
parameters.description: Comma-separated attribute names to omit from the default set.

put.description:
Replaces all attributes of an existing SCIM User resource with the
values in the request body (full replacement, RFC 7644 §3.5.1).
Any attributes omitted from the body are cleared on the server.

400.description: Request body is missing or malformed.

patch.description:
Applies a partial update to a SCIM User resource using PatchOp
(RFC 7644 §3.5.2). Supported operations: `add`, `remove`, `replace`.
The `path` attribute uses SCIM attribute notation including filter
expressions (e.g. `emails[type eq "work"].value`).

400.description: Request body is missing or malformed.

delete.description:
Permanently removes a SCIM User resource. Returns 204 No Content on
success; the response body is empty.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of SCIM Group resources matching the optional
filter. Pagination is controlled by `startIndex` (1-based) and `count`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
SCIM filter expression (RFC 7644 §3.4.2.2), e.g.
`displayName eq "Tour Guides"`.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description: 1-based index of the first result to return.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return per page.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: Comma-separated SCIM attribute names to include.

parameters.name: excludedAttributes
parameters.description: Comma-separated SCIM attribute names to exclude.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Attribute to sort by (parsed but not guaranteed server-side).

post.description:
Creates a new SCIM Group resource. The `displayName` attribute is
required. Returns the created resource with status 201 and a
`Location` header.

Location.description:
URI of the created resource (RFC 7644 section 3.1). Absolute
when `--scim-base-url` is set, prefix-relative otherwise.

400.description: Request body is missing or malformed.

409.description: A group with that displayName already exists.

get.description: Returns a single SCIM Group resource by its server-assigned ID.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description:
Comma-separated attribute names to return, in place of the default
set (RFC 7644 section 3.9). Mutually exclusive with
`excludedAttributes`.

parameters.name: excludedAttributes
parameters.description: Comma-separated attribute names to omit from the default set.

put.description:
Replaces all attributes of an existing SCIM Group resource with the
values in the request body (full replacement, RFC 7644 §3.5.1).

400.description: Request body is missing or malformed.

patch.description:
Applies a partial update to a SCIM Group resource using PatchOp
(RFC 7644 §3.5.2). Typical use-cases: adding or removing members,
renaming the group.

400.description: Request body is missing or malformed.

delete.description:
Permanently removes a SCIM Group resource. Returns 204 No Content on
success; the response body is empty.

post.description:
Executes multiple SCIM operations in a single HTTP request (RFC 7644
§3.7). Operations are processed sequentially. Supports `bulkId`
cross-references: a POST operation with `"bulkId":"abc"` creates a
resource; subsequent operations in the same request can reference it
as `"bulkId:abc"` wherever a SCIM id is expected.

The `failOnErrors` field controls how many errors to tolerate before
aborting. Set to 0 (default) to process all operations regardless of
individual errors.

Maximum payload size and operation count are configurable server-side
(defaults: 1 MiB / 100 operations). Exceeding either returns 413.

200.description: Bulk operations completed (may include per-operation errors).

400.description: Request body is missing, malformed, or exceeds operation count limit.

get.description:
Returns the SCIM 2.0 ServiceProviderConfig document (RFC 7643 §5).
Describes which optional features this server supports: PATCH, Bulk,
filtering, sorting, ETags, and the active authentication schemes.
No authentication is required for this endpoint.

Returns all registered SCIM ResourceType definitions wrapped in a
ListResponse envelope (RFC 7643 §6). This server exposes `User` and
`Group` resource types.

Returns a single SCIM ResourceType definition by its `id` (name).
Supported values: `User`, `Group`.

Returns all SCIM Schema definitions wrapped in a ListResponse envelope
(RFC 7643 §7). Schemas describe the attributes available on User and
Group resources. Schema files are loaded from the server's configured
`schemas_path` (defaults to `static/schemas/scim/`).

Returns a single SCIM Schema definition by its URN identifier.
The `:id` segment must be URL-encoded (the generator extracts it as
a path parameter automatically). Example URNs:
- `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User`
- `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group`

Returns a JSON schema file from the top-level `schemas/` directory
of the configured static path.  The `:name` segment must be made of
alphanumerics and hyphens, in parts joined by single dots, with a
`.json` extension; a name without that extension is served as a
plain static file.

Schema files may contain `__FOO_BAR__` placeholders that are
substituted at serve-time with the value of the corresponding
`--foo-bar` server option, allowing the same file to be used for
both server-side validation and browser-side form rendering. A
schema that `extends` another is served merged with it, and a
schema file of the configuration is served at the `schemaUrl` the
configuration API gives for it, wherever the file is.

500.description: A schema it extends is missing or invalid.

get.description:
Returns a JSON schema from a named sub-directory of `schemas/`.
`:dir` and `:name` follow the rules of the top-level route, and are
validated before the file-system path is resolved, and the
resolved path is checked against the schemas root to prevent
path-traversal attacks.

Available sub-directories depend on the static path configured at
startup.  Typical deployments include `standard`, `twake`, `ad`,
`scim`, and `obm`.

200.description: JSON schema file from the sub-directory.

500.description: A schema it extends is missing or invalid.

get.summary: Get JSON schema from a nested subdirectory
get.description:
Returns a JSON schema from a sub-directory of `schemas/` at any
depth, such as `/static/schemas/twake/nomenclature/twakeTitle.json`,
with the rules of the other schema routes for every segment.

parameters.name: subdir
parameters.description: One or more directories, separated by slashes.

200.description: JSON schema file from the sub-directory.

500.description: A schema it extends is missing or invalid.

get.summary: List app accounts for a user
get.description:
Returns all application-specific accounts belonging to `:user`, where
`:user` is the principal account email (globally unique). Ownership is
resolved by the mail attribute, not the LDAP `uid`, which may repeat
under different subtrees of the directory. The principal account
(whose uid equals the mail address) is always filtered out.

Results are sorted alphabetically by `uid`.

post.summary: Create an app account for a user
post.description:
Creates a new application-specific identity under the configured
applicative-account LDAP branch.  The server generates a random
uid (`<prefix>_c<8-digits>`, prefix derived from `:user`) and a
cryptographically secure password, then:

1. Copies `cn`, `sn`, `givenName`, `mail`, and `displayName` from
   the principal user entry.
2. Adds the cleartext password to the principal account
   (`uid=<mail>`) so single-point authentication still works.

Step 2 is not optional: services bind against the principal account,
so a password absent there would authenticate nowhere. If it fails,
the app account created in step 1 is rolled back and the call returns
`500` rather than a credential that does not work.

Returns a `400` if the user has already reached the server-side
maximum number of app accounts (`max_app_accounts`, default 5).

**The generated password is returned only once** — store it
immediately.

200.description: App account created — includes the one-time password.

400.description: User has no mail attribute or maximum account limit reached.

delete.description:
Deletes the app account identified by `:uid` and removes its
password from the principal account (`uid=<mail>`). `:user` is the
principal account email.

The target account's mail must match `:user` — attempting to delete an
account that belongs to a different principal returns `403`.

The operation is **idempotent**: if the account does not exist,
the response is still `200` with the `uid` echoed back.

Revocation requires reading the account's `userPassword` to know which
of the principal's values to remove. If it cannot be read — typically
a bind DN without read access on `userPassword` in the applicative
branch — or if removing it fails, the account is **kept** and the call
returns `500`, so that the request stays replayable once the cause is
fixed. It never reports a revocation that did not happen.

200.description: App account deleted (or was already absent).

500.description:
The account password could not be read or could not be removed
from the principal account; the app account was left in place.

post.summary: Make sure an account has its workplace instance
post.description:
Writes a missing address and announces the account when its instance
exists, and asks for the instance when it does not. Answers `ready`
once the address is written, `pending` while the instance is built.
The caller reads and writes the account with its own rights.

400.description: Neither a DN nor a mail, or a malformed one.

404.description: No such account the caller can read.

schema.description: The account, by DN or by mail.

get.description:
Returns the current mailbox quota counters (message count and
storage size) for the given user. Requires the Apache James
integration to be configured (`james_webadmin_url`,
`james_webadmin_token`). The quota data is fetched live from
the James WebAdmin API.

400.description: User has no mail attribute configured in LDAP.

example.error: User alice has no mail attribute

404.description: User not found in LDAP, or quota entry absent in James.

502.description: James WebAdmin API is unreachable or returned an error.

example.error: Failed to retrieve quota from James: Bad Gateway

get.summary: Where the migration proxy routes a user
get.description:
Asks the Twake Mail migration proxy whether the user is on its
migrated list, that is routed to the new backend. The user is
found by `uid` across the directory and answered only when the
caller can read the entry.

404.description: User not found, or not readable by the caller.

502.description: The proxy is unreachable or answered an error.

post.description:
Removes a deleted account for good, with its group memberships. The
deletion must be older than `--twake-tombstone-erase-min-age`, unless
`force` is true. Nothing is published.

409.description: The deletion is too recent and `force` is not set.

get.description:
Returns all entries in the flat LDAP branch, keyed by their
`mainAttribute` value (e.g. `uid` for users). The optional
`match` and `attribute` query parameters filter results using
a substring LDAP search (`attribute=*match*`). `attribute` accepts
several names separated by commas, and the clauses are then joined
with `|`. The `attributes`
parameter limits which LDAP attributes are returned.

Without `limit`, the answer holds every match or fails: a directory
whose size limit is below the number of matches makes it a `422`.
With `limit`, at most that many entries come back, and the
`X-Result-Truncated: true` header says others were left out.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description:
Plural name of the flat resource (e.g. `users`, `mailgroups`).
Each concrete plugin sets its own value.

parameters.name: match
parameters.description:
Substring to match. Must be used together with `attribute`.
The resulting LDAP filter is `(attribute=*match*)`, or
`(|(a=*match*)(b=*match*))` when several attributes are named.

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description:
LDAP attribute name to match against (used with `match`).
Several may be given, separated by commas; an entry matching any
of them is returned. Each name must be indexed for a substring
search, or the directory scans the branch.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of LDAP attributes to include in each
returned entry. Omit to return all attributes. The
`mainAttribute` is always returned: it keys the map.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Return at most this many entries. When more match, the response
carries `X-Result-Truncated: true`. It also does when the
directory refused to list every match, even if fewer than
`limit` came back: the directory does not say whether it cut
that answer short.

200.description: Map of entries keyed by mainAttribute value.

X-Result-Truncated.description:
`true` when `limit` was given and the answer may not hold
every match (see `limit`). Absent otherwise.

400.description:
Invalid LDAP attribute name in `attribute` parameter, or `limit`
is not a positive integer.

422.description:
No `limit` was given and more entries match than the directory
will list in one answer (LDAP `sizeLimitExceeded`).

example.error: Too many entries to list at once: the directory's size limit was exceeded. Narrow the search, or pass `limit`.

post.description:
Creates a new entry in the flat LDAP branch. The `mainAttribute`
field (e.g. `uid`) is required and used to construct the DN.
Returns the newly created entry on success (HTTP 201).

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description:
Plural name of the flat resource (e.g. `users`, `mailgroups`).
Each concrete plugin sets its own value.

201.description: Entry created; returns the new entry.

400.description: Missing required field or validation error.

get.summary: Get entry by ID or DN
get.description:
Returns a single entry identified by its `mainAttribute` value
(e.g. a `uid`) or by its full DN. If the value starts with
`mainAttribute=` it is treated as a DN; otherwise it is treated
as a raw RDN value.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description:
Plural name of the flat resource (e.g. `users`, `mailgroups`).
Each concrete plugin sets its own value.

400.description: The supplied DN is not a direct child of the configured base.

delete.description:
Permanently removes the entry identified by `id` from the LDAP
branch. The `id` may be either a `mainAttribute` value or the
entry's full DN.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description:
Plural name of the flat resource (e.g. `users`, `mailgroups`).
Each concrete plugin sets its own value.

put.description:
Applies a partial update to the entry identified by `id`. The
body follows the LDAP modify structure: `add`, `replace`, and/or
`delete` maps. The `mainAttribute` (e.g. `uid`) cannot be
changed through this endpoint.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description:
Plural name of the flat resource (e.g. `users`, `mailgroups`).
Each concrete plugin sets its own value.

400.description: Validation error or attempt to modify a fixed attribute.

post.description:
Moves the entry to a different organisational unit by updating
the configured department-link and department-path attributes
(`ldap_organization_link_attribute` and
`ldap_organization_path_attribute`). The plugin's schema must
declare both attributes; otherwise the request is rejected with
400.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description:
Plural name of the flat resource (e.g. `users`, `mailgroups`).
Each concrete plugin sets its own value.

200.description: Entry moved; returns the new department path and link.

400.description:
Missing or invalid `targetOrgDn`, or schema does not support
the move operation.

404.description: Entry or target organisation not found.

post.description:
Changes the `mainAttribute` value of the entry — its RDN, and so its
DN — and rewrites the references other entries hold to the old DN:
group memberships and ownerships, delegations, managers, every
pointer a loaded schema declares towards this branch. The rewrite is
finished when the call returns.

The body field is `newId` for every resource, whatever that resource
calls its `mainAttribute`, and it carries a value, not a DN.

The new value is held to the same `test` as a creation would hold it
to, and refused when the identifier is already taken in this branch.
A `unique` constraint the schema widens to other branches is **not**
applied here: it is enforced from the add and modify hooks, while
what a rename needs is the RDN's own branch — which is the namespace
the directory itself enforces.

Re-issuing the same rename is a repair, not an error: when the entry
already carries the new identifier, the reference rewrite runs alone.
That is how a `207` is finished off.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description:
Plural name of the flat resource (e.g. `users`, `mailgroups`).
Each concrete plugin sets its own value.

200.description: Entry renamed and every reference rewritten.

207.description:
Entry renamed, but at least one reference could not be
rewritten. The rename is done and is not rolled back; re-issue
the same request to finish the rewrite.

400.description:
Missing or invalid `newId`, a value the schema refuses, or an
attribute sent beside it.

403.description: No write permission on the branch.

Config.description:
Aggregated server configuration. `apiPrefix`, `ldapBase` and
`features` are always present; `version` is present unless the server
could not read it at start-up; `features` is a dynamic map whose keys
are the names of loaded plugins that declare the `configurable` role.
Each plugin contributes an arbitrary sub-object — consult the
individual plugin documentation for its exact shape.

apiPrefix.description: The API base path configured on this server.

ldapBase.description: The root LDAP suffix used by this server.

version.description:
The server's version, as its package declares it. A client reads it
to tell an administrator the server is older than it supports; a
server that cannot tell its version leaves the field out.

features.description:
Per-plugin configuration blocks.  Keys match the plugin's
`name` field; values are plugin-specific objects.

BulkImportResult.description: Summary returned after a bulk import operation.

success.description: True when no fatal error aborted the import early.

total.description: Total number of CSV data rows (excluding header).

created.description: Entries successfully created (or that would be, in a dry run).

updated.description: Existing entries updated (or that would be, in a dry run).

skipped.description: Existing entries skipped because `updateExisting` was false.

line.description: 1-based CSV line number (2 = first data row).

identifier.description: Value of the main attribute for the failing row (if known).

dn.description: Fully-qualified distinguished name of the entry.

cn.description: Common name (RDN attribute) of the group.
Common name of the new group.

GroupModify.description:
Partial update. Each provided attribute is replaced wholesale. Use
the dedicated `/members` endpoints to add/remove members one at a
time without supplying the full list.

code.description:
For a client to explain the refusal in its own words, when there
is one: `unique` (a value already used), `mailDomain` (an address
outside the authorised mail domains), `forbidden` (the caller may
not act on this branch). Absent for any other refusal, which only
`error` describes. The Twake groups API answers its own codes
(`INVALID_INPUT`, `REFUSED`…).

example.error: entity: "value" is already used (attribute must be unique)

dn.description: Fully-qualified distinguished name of the entry.

organizationLink.description: DN of the parent organization (link attribute).

organizationPath.description:
Human-readable slash-separated path to this node, used by the
UI tree. Set automatically on creation and move.

member.description: DNs of entries linked to this organization.

OrgSummary.description: Lightweight organization reference (used in node lists).

ou.description: Name of the new organizational unit.

parentDn.description:
DN of the parent organizational unit. Defaults to the configured
top organization when omitted.

OrganizationModify.description:
Partial update. Any provided attribute is replaced wholesale.
`ou` cannot be changed via this endpoint — use the move endpoint
to relocate the node within the tree.

PasswordPolicy.description:
Active OpenLDAP ppolicy configuration. All duration fields are in
**seconds**. Absent fields mean the policy attribute is not set.

pwdMaxAge.description: Maximum password age in seconds (0 = never expires).

pwdMinAge.description: Minimum password age in seconds before it may be changed.

pwdLockoutDuration.description: Lockout duration in seconds (0 = permanent until admin reset).

pwdGraceAuthNLimit.description: Number of grace logins allowed after password expires.

pwdExpireWarning.description: Seconds before expiry at which a warning is issued.

pwdMustChange.description: If true, users must change their password after an admin reset.

pwdAllowUserChange.description: Whether users are allowed to change their own password.

PasswordStatus.description: Current password status for a specific user account.

passwordSet.description: Whether a userPassword attribute is present.

lastChanged.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of last password change, or null if never set.

expiresAt.description: ISO-8601 expiry timestamp, or null if no max age is configured.

daysUntilExpiration.description: Remaining days until expiry (negative means already expired).

isExpiringSoon.description: True when expiry is within the configured warning window.

mustChange.description: True when `pwdReset` is set (admin forced change).

isLocked.description: True when the account is currently locked.

lockedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of lockout, or null.

failureCount.description: Number of recorded bind failures still within the window.

graceLoginsUsed.description: Number of grace logins already consumed.

policy.description:
DN of the policy the status was computed with: the one the
account's `pwdPolicySubentry` names, else the default one.

PasswordPolicyEntry.description:
A password policy entry. Only the attributes the entry holds are
served; durations are in **seconds**. `pwdAttribute` and
`pwdCheckModule` are read-only.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the policy accounts without `pwdPolicySubentry` get.

pwdCheckModuleArg.description: Configuration of the quality-check module, usually several lines.

PasswordPolicyChanges.description:
Attributes to set, by name as in `PasswordPolicyEntry`. `null` removes
the attribute. On `PATCH`, `dn`, `cn`, `isDefault` and the read-only
attributes are accepted only with the value the entry already has.

ExpiringAccount.description: User whose password is expiring within the warning window.

LockedAccount.description: User account that is currently locked.

dn.description: Optional user DN for context (not used in local validation).

valid.description: True when the password meets all complexity rules.

errors.description: List of failed rule descriptions (empty when valid).

RawAttribute.description:
Values of a single attribute. When `binary` is true the values are
base64-encoded octets rather than text.

RawEntry.description: A directory entry with all its attributes, as stored.

RawChild.description: Direct child of an entry, as needed to draw a tree node.

hasChildren.description:
Whether the entry has at least one child. Only computed when the
`children` query parameter is set, otherwise always false.

startIndex.description: 1-based index of the first result returned.

itemsPerPage.description: Number of resources returned in this page.

status.description: HTTP status code as a string.

scimType.description:
SCIM error type keyword (RFC 7644 §3.12). One of: invalidFilter,
tooMany, uniqueness, mutability, invalidSyntax, invalidPath,
noTarget, invalidValue, invalidVers, sensitive.

value.description: New value for the target attribute.

failOnErrors.description:
Stop processing after this many errors. Omit or set to 0 to
continue on errors and process all operations.

bulkId.description:
Temporary client-assigned identifier for this operation.
Subsequent operations in the same request may reference the
created resource as "bulkId:<value>".

path.description: Resource path relative to the SCIM prefix (e.g. /Users or /Groups/123).

status.description: HTTP status code for this individual operation.

response.description: Present only when the operation failed.

LdapSchema.description:
A JSON schema file served from the `schemas/` sub-directory of the
static path.  These schemas describe LDAP entity types (users, groups,
organizations, …) and are consumed by browser-embedded editors to
render attribute forms and validate input before submission.

The server replaces `__FOO_BAR__` placeholders on the fly with the
value of the corresponding `--foo-bar` CLI option so that a single
schema file can be shared between server-side validation and
client-side rendering. A schema that `extends` another is served
merged with it.

AppAccount.description:
An application-specific identity attached to a user.  App accounts
allow a single principal user to authenticate as different named
"devices" or "applications" each with its own credential, while
sharing the same mail address.

uid.description:
Unique identifier of the app account.  Format:
`<prefix>_c<8-digits>`, where `<prefix>` is the `:user` path param
(the resolution value — the mail by default) sanitized into a
uid-safe token (e.g. `alice@example.com` -> `alice_example_com`).

AppAccountCreated.description:
Response returned when a new app account is successfully created.
The one-time cleartext password is included here and never returned
again — callers must store it immediately.

uid.description: Identifier of the newly created app account.

pwd.description:
One-time cleartext password generated for this account.
Format: 6 blocks of 4 characters separated by `-`
(e.g. `Ab3@-xYz!-9pQ#-Sv4$-mN8!-pQ5@`).
OpenLDAP hashes it via ppolicy before storage.

mail.description: Mail address of the principal account this app account belongs to.

AppAccountCreate.description: Request body for creating a new app account.

name.description: Optional human-readable label for the new account.

JamesQuotaUsage.description:
Quota information for a mailbox user as returned by the James
WebAdmin API (`GET /quota/users/{mail}`). Contains separate
counters for message count and storage size.

max.description: Maximum number of messages allowed. `null` means unlimited.

FlatEntry.description:
A single LDAP entry from a flat branch. The `dn` field is always
present; all other fields depend on the concrete plugin's schema
(e.g. `uid`, `cn`, `mail`, `sn` for users).

dn.description: Fully-qualified distinguished name of the entry.

FlatList.description:
A map of entries returned by the LIST endpoint, keyed by the
entry's `mainAttribute` value (e.g. the `uid` for users). This
is the `LdapList` shape (`Record<string, FlatEntry>`).

FlatCreate.description:
Body for creating a new entry. The plugin's `mainAttribute` field
(e.g. `uid`) is required and used to build the DN. All other
attributes are plugin-specific; unknown attributes are accepted
unless the plugin's schema is in strict mode.

FlatModify.description:
Partial-update body. Supports `add`, `replace`, and `delete`
maps matching the LDAP modify operation. The `mainAttribute`
(e.g. `uid`) cannot be changed through this endpoint — use the
rename API instead.

replace.description: Attributes whose values are replaced wholesale.

delete.description:
Attributes (or specific values) to remove. Either an array
of attribute names or a map of attribute → value(s).

FlatMoveRequest.description:
Body for moving an entry to a different organisational unit.
Requires `ldap_organization_link_attribute` and
`ldap_organization_path_attribute` to be defined in the plugin's
schema.

targetOrgDn.description: DN of the destination organisational unit.

FlatRenameRequest.description:
Body for changing the identifier of an entry. The field is named
`newId` for every resource, whatever that resource calls its
`mainAttribute`.

newId.description: New value of the resource's `mainAttribute`. A value, not a DN.

FlatRenameResult.description:
Outcome of a rename: the entry's new DN, and how many references to
the old one were rewritten.

success.description: False when a reference could not be rewritten.

referencesUpdated.description: References rewritten to the new DN.

referencesFailed.description:
References left naming the old DN, counted per attribute. The
referring entries are named in the server log, not here.
